newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-STRANG TAKES SIX WICKETS IN KENT WIN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-STRANG TAKES SIX WICKETS IN KENT WIN.

text.p: Zimbabwean leg spinner Paul Strang finished with six wickets as Kent squeezed out a four-run county championship victory over Middlesex at Lord's on Friday.
Strang added four scalps to the two he claimed on Thursday for a six for 88 return.
Kent's win was particularly tough on Middlesex captain Mark Ramprakash who made an unbeaten 113 after his side began the day 134 for five -- 127 short of their victory target.
When Jacques Kallis and Keith Brown were out in successive overs for the addition of only 23 runs Kent looked home and dry.
But first Richard Johnson and then Angus Fraser helped their skipper push Middlesex to within 25 of their target.
They were almost steered home by the last wicket pair of Ramprakash and Phil Tufnell. But Tufnell eventually popped up a catch to Trevor Ward at silly mid-off.
Chris Tolley claimed the first hat-trick of his career for Nottinghamshire at Grace Road on an eventful day which ended with Leicestershire set a victory target of 258.
Tolley finished with career-best figures of six for 61 as Leicestershire were dismissed for 267, giving Notts a lead of 75.
But after reaching tea in the reasonably healthy position of 85 for two Notts collapsed to 182 all out.
